reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it primarily presents a step-by-step educational tutorial for installing Phantom, creating a wallet, protecting its recovery phrase, and obtaining a Solana address. Although it discusses tokenized stocks, yield, borrowing, and transferring SOL for transaction fees, it does not establish guaranteed returns or a deceptive solicitation. The speaker also warns against scam download links and presents the material as informational with an explicit risk disclaimer.

citations.quote: How to Set Up a Phantom Wallet on Solana (Beginner's Guide)
I'm going to walk you through exactly how to set up a Phantom wallet step by step
you probably want to send at least 20 worth of soul because that's the gas that you're going to need in order to buy things
You'll be able to earn yield on those stocks and even borrow against them.
this phrase is the only way to recover your wallet. Do not share this with anyone

opening.argument: The tutorial does more than explain wallet mechanics: it presents funding the wallet as the gateway to financial activities and yield. Viewers are told that, once they have a wallet, they can earn yield on stocks and borrow against them, while the instructions then direct them to obtain SOL and transfer it to the wallet for transaction fees. That links a concrete money-flow action to promised access to yield-generating participation. The step-by-step format makes the path unusually actionable: create the wallet, acquire SOL, and send funds onward. Even without an explicit guarantee, presenting yield as an immediate capability after funding can encourage viewers to treat the setup as a route to returns.

citations.quote: You'll be able to earn yield on those stocks and even borrow against them.
you probably want to send at least 20 worth of soul because that's the gas that you're going to need in order to buy things
Once your Phantom wallet is set up, you'll be able to buy tokenized stocks like Tesla, Apple, and Nvidia 24/7, earn yield on your holdings, swap tokens, and access the entire Solana DeFi ecosystem.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not answer the financial linkage. The defense quotes wallet-creation instructions and recovery-phrase warnings, but those explain only the mechanics. The same presentation expressly connects setup and funding with buying tokenized stocks and earning yield. The absence of a guaranteed-return sentence does not remove the promotional implication that depositing SOL opens access to lucrative financial activity.

citations.quote: Once you have a wallet, you'll be able to do things most people don't even know are possible.
you probably want to send at least 20 worth of soul because that's the gas that you're going to need in order to buy things

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Those quotations show access and transaction funding, not a promised return from a pool, lending arrangement, or staking program. The video says viewers can earn yield on stocks, but it does not specify a fixed, passive, or compounding return, nor does it require participation in a managed investment. The funding instruction is for network gas, and the material is explicitly presented as informational rather than a financial guarantee.

citations.quote: Disclaimer: This video is for info only, not financial advice. Crypto trading involves risk, do your own research before trading.
it's very cheap to transact on solana
You'll be able to earn yield on those stocks and even borrow against them.

opening.argument: Several risk signals appear together: crypto wallet creation, external links, instructions to buy and transfer digital assets, and a stated 30-40% yield-farming opportunity involving tokenized stocks. The return figure is not isolated in unrelated commentary; it appears in the same series that begins by directing viewers to set up and fund a Phantom wallet. The description also says the wallet will enable buying named tokenized stocks and earning yield. This combination can make a high-return financial pathway look routine and beginner-friendly, while the practical steps normalize moving money into the ecosystem. The disclaimer does not neutralize the stronger impression created by the return figure and multiple calls to follow links and continue to later videos.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the risk disclaimer and scam-download warning as if they explain away the financial promotion. They do not address the advertised 30-40% yield-farming range or the description's promise of yield after wallet setup. Nor does calling the video a beginner guide explain why viewers are directed toward external services, a free guide, and a funded wallet. Those signals are relevant precisely because the presentation lowers the perceived difficulty of entering a speculative tokenized-stock activity.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The 30-40% wording is a title for a later video, not a demonstrated return, guarantee, or result in this wallet-setup tutorial. The present material shows how to install and fund a wallet; it does not establish that tokenized stocks appreciate, pay dividends, or produce the stated range. It also warns viewers about scams and expressly says crypto trading involves risk and requires research.

Part 1: How to Set Up a Phantom Wallet
Crypto trading involves risk, do your own research before trading.

opening.argument: The educational wrapper functions as a funnel into tokenized-stock and DeFi participation. The speaker presents wallet setup as the necessary first step, then directs viewers to download Phantom, buy SOL, transfer assets, obtain a free blueprint, and watch a follow-up showing how to buy Tesla and Nvidia without a broker. That is more than neutral explanation: the instructional sequence steers a beginner toward a specific crypto ecosystem and named financial products. The description reinforces the commercial pathway by listing tokenized stocks, yield, swaps, multiple service links, and a multi-part series. Framing these steps as a simple beginner tutorial can make the underlying investment promotion appear merely operational.

in my next video, I'm going to show you something most people don't know is possible. How to buy Tesla, Nvidia and other major stocks, 24 7 with no broker using your Solana wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense focuses on the presence of operational instructions, but that is exactly what makes the promotional role effective. The video does not merely describe wallets in the abstract: it supplies a download route, tells viewers how to fund the wallet, offers a blueprint, and previews stock purchases using that wallet. A disclaimer and a warning about scam links do not change the fact that the tutorial directs viewers into a particular tokenized-stock pathway.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited steps establish a wallet tutorial and a preview of a separate topic, not that viewers are promised appreciation, dividends, or profits from buying tokenized products. Naming Tesla and Nvidia describes the proposed use case; it does not show an investment outcome. The material also labels itself informational and warns that trading involves risk, which is inconsistent with presenting participation as risk-free or guaranteed.
